_metadata.variant: 912 i Series (912 iS, 912 iS Sport, 912 iSc Sport)
_metadata.om_reference: OM-912 i Series, Edition 2 / Rev. 2, September 01 2025
_metadata.om_chapter: Chapter 2.1 Operating Limits (pages 2-2 to 2-4); warm-up Chapter 3.5; cold-start oil pressure Chapter 4.17
_metadata.notes: All limit values sourced directly from the Operators Manual except bus voltage (not an OM limit), fuel_press_max phase durations (operational suppression inherited from the 916iS profile, not an OM value) and phase_detection (derived). Naturally aspirated: no manifold pressure limit and no EGT split limit exist in this OM, so there is no map_max limit and no egt_spread block — do not add them. The 'overboost' block is kept only because the limit checker reads it for the 5-minute take-off RPM rule; the name is a misnomer for this engine. Do not modify without updating om_reference.

_expected_hot_cylinder_note: Spec 08 §3: prior for the usual hottest cylinder until an aircraft's own is learned; a display hint, never a limit. No turbo, so no expected pattern.
_rated_power_note: Take-off 73.5 kW (100 hp) at 5,800 rpm for all three variants. Max continuous differs by variant: 912 iS 69 kW (93 hp), 912 iS Sport / iSc Sport 72 kW (97 hp), all at 5,500 rpm (OM 2.1 Performance table).
_exceedance_merge_gap_s_note: Spec 09 §6.2: an exceedance event ends only after the reading has stayed within the limit this many seconds; shorter dips are absorbed into the event.

limits.label: Idle RPM minimum
limits._exceedance_merge_gap_s_note: Spec 09 Q3: no merging — min_duration_s 30 exists to ignore brief governor dips, and merging would join them into long events.
limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine at or above 1,000 rpm, so a stopped engine (0 rpm before start or after shutdown) isn't an idle exceedance — same gate as fuel_press_min. Note the 912iS idle floor (1,400) is much closer to this gate than the 916iS (1,800).
limits.note: Idle speed min. 1,400 rpm (OM 2.1 Engine speed). Short dips are normal variation.

limits.label: Takeoff RPM (5-min limit)
limits.note: 5,800 rpm is the absolute ceiling, never permitted; the 5-minute allowance above 5,500 rpm is the overboost limit

limits.label: Oil pressure min (>3500 rpm)
limits._filter_policy_note: Spec 09 Q1: the most direct sign of lubrication failure — never filterable.

filter_policy.reason: Low oil pressure at power is the most direct sign of a lubrication problem, so it is always reported. If you suspect the sender or gauge, have it checked rather than filtering the reading.

limits.note: Normal 2.0 to 5.0 bar (29 to 73 psi) above 3,500 rpm (OM 2.1 Oil pressure). Phase-filtered — pre-flight and engine start readings excluded.

limits.label: Oil pressure min (<3500 rpm)

filter_policy.reason: 0.8 bar is the absolute floor at any running speed. A reading below it with the engine running is always reported.

limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine running (at or above 1,000 rpm) so pre-start / post-shutdown zeros aren't events. Applies at every running speed — above 3,500 rpm oil_press_min (29 psi) is the tighter limit.
limits.note: Min. 0.8 bar (12 psi) below 3,500 rpm (OM 2.1 Oil pressure). Absolute floor for a running engine.

limits.label: Oil pressure max (>3500 rpm)
limits.note: Normal 2.0 to 5.0 bar (29 to 73 psi) above 3,500 rpm (OM 2.1 Oil pressure)

limits.label: Oil pressure max (cold start)
limits.note: Max. 7 bar (102 psi), for a short period admissible at cold start (OM 2.1 Oil pressure; OM 4.17 'up to around 7 bar (101.5 psi) does not indicate a malfunction')

limits.label: Oil temp minimum (takeoff)
limits.note: Oil temperature min. 50°C (OM 2.1 prints 120°F; 50°C = 122°F, and OM 3.5 warm-up gives 50°C / 122°F). Warm up until oil reaches 50°C before run-up. Phase-filtered — pre-flight readings excluded.

limits.label: Oil temp maximum
limits.note: Max. 130°C / 266°F (OM 2.1 Oil temperature). Note: higher than the 915/916 limit of 120°C.

limits.label: Oil temp normal band (low)
limits.note: Normal operating temperature approx. 90 to 110°C (OM 2.1 prints 190 to 230°F; 90°C = 194°F). Reported in oil temp analysis section, not exceedances.

limits.label: Fuel pressure minimum
limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine at or above 1,000 rpm: with the engine stopped the fuel pumps are off and the reading falls to 0 psi. RPM gate rather than phase list because phase labels can't be relied on at the end of a log (Spec 09 §16).
limits.note: Fuel pressure at fuel rail min. 2.8 bar / 40.61 psi (OM 2.1 Fuel pressure). Exceedance down to 2.5 bar / 36 psi acceptable for max. 3 sec after a power setting change.

limits.label: Fuel pressure maximum
limits._min_duration_by_phase_note: Operational suppression carried over from the 916iS profile (pump tests in taxi, tank switching in cruise) — not an OM value. The OM itself tolerates only 3 sec after a power change; these durations are deliberately looser. Review against real 912iS logs when available.
limits.note: Fuel pressure at fuel rail max. 3.2 bar / 46.41 psi (OM 2.1 Fuel pressure). Exceedance up to 3.5 bar / 51 psi acceptable for max. 3 sec after a power setting change.

limits.label: Bus voltage minimum
limits.note: Not an OM limit. Below ~12V indicates alternator failure or excessive load.

limits.label: Bus voltage maximum
limits.note: Not an OM limit. Above 14.5V indicates voltage regulator fault.

_egt_spread_note: Intentionally absent: OM-912 i Series Chapter 2.1 defines no EGT split / cylinder-difference limit (unlike OM-915/916). The EGT split checker must not run for this engine — see limits.py egt_spread defaults.

overboost.note: Naturally aspirated engine — no boost. Block retained only because it is the single owner of the OM 5-minute take-off rule: 5,800 rpm / 100% power for max. 5 min (OM 2.1 Engine speed).

_eco_power_mode_note: Intentionally absent: the 912iS ECU has ECO and POWER modes but OM-912 i Series Ed.2 Rev.2 states no throttle-position threshold for the switch-over, so none is configured.

phase_detection.note: Values derived from operating limits above — not separately sourced. idle_rpm_min follows the OM idle floor (1,400). OM 3.5/3.6: warm-up at ~2,000 then 2,500 rpm; ignition check at 4,000 rpm; fuel pump check at 2,000 rpm (OM 3.7).
